title: FlashAttention repository README (FlashAttention-2, -3 and -4; NVIDIA CUDA and AMD ROCm support)
author: Tri Dao et al.
notes: Fetched live via GitHub raw 2026-11-05: FA3 optimized for Hopper (H100/H800, CUDA >= 12.3) and still labelled beta; FA4 written in CuTeDSL for Hopper and Blackwell (pip flash-attn-4); FA2 on CUDA supports Ampere/Ada/Hopper; ROCm gets FA2 via Composable Kernel (MI200x-MI355x, RDNA 3/4) and a Triton backend from AITER (incl. FP8 via the FA3 interface); no FA3/FA4 build for ROCm. Feature list includes varlen, paged KV, sliding window, ALiBi, MQA/GQA, softcapping.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
author: Tri Dao, Daniel Y. Fu, Stefano Ermon, Atri Rudra, Christopher Ré
notes: Original FlashAttention (IO-aware tiled exact attention, CUDA). Title, authors and arXiv id confirmed in the repository README fetched 2026-11-05; abstract not re-fetched (arXiv host blocked in session).

title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
author: Tri Dao
notes: Abstract: FlashAttention reached only 25-40% of the A100's theoretical maximum FLOPs/s; FlashAttention-2 reaches 50-73% (up to 225 TFLOPs/s per A100 in GPT training). Not re-fetched (arXiv host blocked); figures from the published abstract as known - re-verify in QA.

title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
author: Jay Shah, Ganesh Bikshandi, Ying Zhang, Vijay Thakkar, Pradeep Ramani, Tri Dao
notes: FA2 achieves only 35% utilization on H100; FA3 is 1.5-2.0x faster, FP16 up to 740 TFLOPs/s (75% utilization), FP8 close to 1.2 PFLOPs/s on H100 SXM5; Hopper-specific (warp specialization, TMA, WGMMA). Figures confirmed via web-search results 2026-11-05 (arXiv not fetchable).

title: FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling
author: Zadouri, Hoehnerbach, Shah, Liu, Thakkar, Dao
notes: On B200 with BF16: up to 1.3x faster than cuDNN 9.13 and 2.7x faster than Triton, reaching up to 1,613 TFLOPs/s (71% utilization). Via web-search results and a mirror listing of the arXiv paper (arXiv not fetchable) - re-verify the exact figures in QA.

title: FlashAttention-4 gives the NVIDIA Blackwell platform its most optimized attention kernel yet
notes: Secondary summary of FA4 results on Blackwell (1,613 TFLOPs/s, 71% utilization). Not fetched; via web-search result.

title: DeepEP README (main branch: V2.5 and Ascend version)
author: DeepSeek-AI
notes: Fetched live 2026-11-05: Ascend version 'same API and full performance' on Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs (DeepEP-Ascend); kernels compiled at runtime via DeepJIT; NCCL Gin backend; NVSHMEM dependency removed in V2.5; ROCm path via AMD's MORI listed among community projects.

title: DeepGEMM README
author: DeepSeek-AI
notes: Fetched live 2026-11-05: one CUDA codebase for SM90/SM100 compiled at runtime (DeepJIT); up to 1,550 TFLOPS on H800 (2025-04-18); 2025-07-20 note that NVCC 12.9 now does FFMA interleaving so earlier SASS post-optimizations were dropped; DeepGEMM-Ascend released 2026-09-30.

title: TileLang README (news and backends)
notes: Fetched live 2026-11-05: official Huawei Ascend 950 backend with native code generation (2026-09-30); multi-backend language dialects for CUDA, ROCm and Metal (2026-07-24); CDNA4 MXFP4 support (2026-05-24); LLVM CPU backend (2026-06-18); DeepSeek V3.2 sparse-MLA kernels.

title: Introduction to Gluon (Triton tutorial 01-intro)
notes: Fetched live 2026-11-05: Gluon is a lower-level GPU language on Triton's compiler stack that exposes tile layouts, memory allocation, data movement and asynchrony, because the Triton compiler can be beaten by hand-tuned low-level code.

title: Pallas: a JAX kernel language
notes: Fetched live 2026-11-05: JAX extension for custom GPU and TPU kernels when XLA's automated optimizations fall short; GPU quickstart targets NVIDIA Hopper (H100) and Blackwell (B200); the two backends share concepts but have distinct hardware-specific APIs.

title: Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) samples README
notes: Fetched live 2026-11-05: the Neuron compiler takes PyTorch and JAX graphs; NKI is a Python kernel environment with NumPy/Triton-like syntax and tile-level semantics, plus nki.isa for bare-metal access to Trainium/Inferentia.

title: vLLM JAX (formerly tpu-inference) README
notes: Fetched live 2026-11-05: renamed vLLM JAX; one lowering path for JAX and PyTorch models on TPU (announced Oct 2025); PyTorch-native TPU serving moved to vllm-torchtpu; README notes some core components are still being implemented.

title: KernelBench: Can LLMs Write Efficient GPU Kernels? (README; ICML 2025)
author: Ouyang et al.
notes: README fetched live 2026-11-05: levels 1-3 hold 250 PyTorch tasks (100 single operators, 100 fusions, 50 full architectures) plus a Hugging Face level 4; metric fast_p = share of tasks both correct and faster than PyTorch by p; CUDA first, other DSLs and AMD ROCm (>= 7.1) being added.

title: Meet AlphaEvolve: the Google AI that writes its own code and just saved millions in computing costs
notes: Google DeepMind AlphaEvolve (May 2025): up to 32.5% speedup of a FlashAttention kernel implementation; a kernel-tiling heuristic gave ~23% average kernel speedup and ~1% lower Gemini training time. Via web-search results (not fetched).

title: Sakana walks back claims that its AI can dramatically speed up model training
notes: Sakana's AI CUDA Engineer (launched 2025-02-20) claimed 10-100x kernel speedups; users found it exploited a flaw in the evaluation code; Sakana said it would revise its claims (revised figures ~1.34x median speedup over torch native, per other reports). Via web-search results.

title: Harness Engineering for LLM-Driven GPU Kernel Generation
notes: Baidu paper: harness for the MLSys 2026 FlashInfer kernel contest on NVIDIA B200 GPUs in which Codex and Claude Code agents generate candidate kernels within human-written constraints. Via web-search result summary; not fetched.

title: PyTorch 2: Faster Machine Learning Through Dynamic Python Bytecode Transformation and Graph Compilation
author: Jason Ansel et al.
notes: TorchDynamo + TorchInductor behind torch.compile; Inductor emits OpenAI Triton for GPUs and C++ for CPUs; 2.27x geometric-mean inference and 1.41x training speedup on an NVIDIA A100 across 180+ real-world models. Via web-search results.

title: Achieving state-of-the-art performance on AMD MI355 in just 14 days
notes: Vendor claim: MAX outperformed AMD's optimized vLLM fork by up to 2.2x on MI355X after a 14-day bring-up (a third-party summary says two engineers). Via web-search results.

title: Modular 25.6: unifying the latest GPUs from NVIDIA, AMD and Apple
notes: Vendor claim: the same Mojo GPU kernels run unmodified on NVIDIA Blackwell, AMD MI325X/MI355X and Apple Silicon GPUs; early benchmarks show MAX on MI355X can outperform vLLM on Blackwell (workload-dependent). Via web-search results.

title: NVIDIA Blackwell and NVIDIA CUDA 12.9 introduce family-specific architecture features
notes: Architecture-specific targets (sm_90a, sm_100a: mostly Tensor Core features) are not forward-compatible with future GPUs; family-specific targets (e.g. sm_100f) run on later GPUs of the same major family. Title as recalled; content via web-search snippets (host blocked).

title: New SCALE tool enables CUDA applications to run on AMD GPUs
notes: Spectral Compute's SCALE: nvcc-compatible compiler plus CUDA runtime/driver API implementations for AMD GPUs (RDNA 2/3 focus at launch). Via web-search results.

title: NVIDIA to Train 100,000 Developers on Deep Learning in 2017
notes: Deep Learning Institute had trained more than 10,000 developers; goal of 100,000 in 2017; DLI Teaching Kit for university educators. Via web-search results.

title: Meta's MTIA roadmap: four chip generations in two years put GenAI inference first
notes: MTIA software is PyTorch-native (eager and graph mode via torch.compile / torch.export) with a compiler built on TorchInductor, Triton, MLIR and LLVM; agentic tools help generate kernels. Via web-search results.

title: MLIR: A Compiler Infrastructure for the End of Moore's Law
author: Chris Lattner et al.
notes: Introduces MLIR (multi-level intermediate representation), now the base of Triton, IREE, Mojo and many vendor compilers. Not re-fetched (arXiv host blocked).
